description: A rotary axis word.
A key given twice on one line, even with the same value.
An annotation must be a line of its own; one in a comment after G-code is malformed.
A comment that starts with GOLIATH in another letter case is a malformed annotation, not a plain comment.
An annotation starts with ;GOLIATH at column 1, with no space after the semicolon.
A quoted value without its closing quote.
I or J on a G0 or G1 move.
K: arcs lie in the XY plane only.
Red-team RT30: the end is 0.004 mm from the start. A full circle or a 0.0046-degree arc? Ambiguous (0 < |end - start| < 0.01 mm): refused (PHYS-16).
End 0.009 mm from the start: still below 0.01 mm, refused.
An arc with neither I nor J.
R-form arc: the centre must be given by I and J.
Start radius 50.000, end radius 50.010: they differ by more than 0.005 mm.
I0 J0: an arc of zero radius.
C (the robot heading) is chosen by goliath-prep; force a heading with OP c= instead.
The decimal separator is a point (spec 05: InvariantCulture).
origin=t1-corner says X = 0, Y = 0 is the panel's tower-1 corner; a job.toml that places the program 100 mm along X disagrees.
STOCK t=18.0005 against T = 18: a difference of 0.0005 mm is a disagreement (values agree only when they differ by less than 0.0005 mm).
Red-team RT27 (part): STOCK t=18.000 from the CAM against the callipers' T = 17.6 in job.toml. Neither wins: refused naming both.
STOCK x=2400.000 against job.toml panel W = 2440: refused naming both values and sources.
STOCK y=1250.000 against job.toml panel H = 1220.
TOOL d=8.000 against job.toml tool diameter 6.
TOOL flute=32.000 against job.toml flute length 22.
TOOL rpm=16000 against job.toml rpm 18000 (compared because both declare it).
TOOL stickout=45.000 against job.toml stick-out 40 (compared because both declare it).
Red-team RT27 (part): TOWER2 axis=X against job.toml tower 2 along Y.
zzero=bottom in GI against z_zero = top in job.toml.
A coordinate beyond 10 000 mm.
The same letter twice on one line.
M2 or M30 stands alone on its line (an N word and a comment are allowed); motion on the same line is refused.
No exponents.
G18: the XY plane only.
G20 (inches): set the CAM to millimetres.
G28: no machine homing moves.
G4 dwell: refused while its gate (drop_dwells, rung R4) is closed, which is always at the desk.
G41: cutter compensation belongs in the CAM.
G55: G54 is the only work offset (a no-op).
G81: canned cycles are expanded by the CAM or the post.
G90.1: arc centres are incremental I/J only; decimal G codes are not in GI.
G91: GI is absolute only.
G92: no coordinate offsets; the origin is the tower-1 corner.
A header line (ZSHIFT) after the header has ended at the first OP line.
origin=centre: GI 1 knows only t1-corner.
zzero=surface: GI 1 knows top and bottom.
STOCK twice, even with equal values: each header line appears once.
STOCK without the thickness t: required, never defaulted.
TOOL without the diameter d: required, never defaulted.
No SOURCE line. A missing required header line is reported at the line that ends the header (here the first OP line).
No STOCK line. A missing required header line is reported at the line that ends the header (here the first OP line).
No TOOL line. A missing required header line is reported at the line that ends the header (here the first OP line).
No TOWER2 line. A missing required header line is reported at the line that ends the header (here the first OP line).
No UNITS line. A missing required header line is reported at the line that ends the header (here the first OP line).
A stock thickness must be greater than zero.
A number is written bare; a quoted number is a type error.
SOURCE needs both cam and post.
kind=chamfer is not one of flat, ball, bull, vbit, other (an unknown value, not an unknown key, so it is refused).
Tower 2 stands along X or Y.
A tool diameter must be greater than zero.
ZSHIFT takes one positional number.
A number has at least one digit before its point.
Word letters are upper case.
M0: nothing can resume a paused program from the host on firmware 01.02.00.
M10 is the robot dialect's spindle on (spec 05); GI writes M3 and goliath-prep translates it.
M11 (dust discharge) is dialect only.
M4: the spindle turns one way.
A ;S empty-the-dust-bin marker (spec 03).
A comment whose first non-blank character is U or S in either case counts as a marker, so this innocent-looking comment is refused: start comments with another character.
A marker in a comment after G-code on the same line.
Red-team RT31 (part): a ;U tool-change marker (spec 03). Outside dialect verify mode, which a GI file never is, it is refused naming the line, not dropped.
Motion after M2.
Red-team RT31 (part): motion after M30. The program has ended; what follows is refused, not dropped.
A negative feed.
A negative spindle speed.
An axis word before any G0, G1, G2 or G3 has set a motion mode.
An en dash instead of a minus sign (a copy-paste error): non-ASCII outside a comment, named by line and column.
In a file with OP blocks, a move below the stock top outside every block belongs to no operation.
Two operations with the same id.
OPEND names a different id than the open OP.
OPEND with no open OP.
Forced heading c=45 is off the 10-degree grid of spec 08 (the vendor's search finds no candidate).
Forced heading c=370 is outside 0..360.
kind=spiral is not one of profile, pocket, drill, engrave, adaptive, other.
OP without an id.
An OP inside an open OP: operations do not nest.
An OP never closed by its OPEND: reported at the OP line.
through takes auto, 1 or 0.
tool=2 names no declared TOOL.
The first motion is outside every OP block while Z is still unknown: an unknown Z counts as possibly below the stock top, never as safe.
Parenthesised comments are not part of GI; comments start with a semicolon.
A % program sentinel: not part of GI.
A second TOOL line: one tool per program.
A word's letter and number are written together.
Any word after M30 is refused, not only motion (the safest reading of PHYS-17).
T and M6 after the first motion, even naming the same tool: a tool change during the program.
T2 names a tool the header does not declare (TOOL n=1).
A point is followed by at least one digit.
At most one M word per line, so the order of actions is never ambiguous.
Two motion codes on one line.
GI 1 is millimetres only: set the CAM to millimetres.
The version is a whole number written without a point or leading zeros.
GOLIATH annotations without a version line: the file is GI and must start with ;GOLIATH-GI 1, so it is refused at line 1 (not read as generic G-code with its annotations ignored).
The version line must be line 1; here a comment precedes it. Reported at line 1.
Version 2 is unknown to a version 1 reader: refused, not guessed.
STOCK t=18.0004 against job.toml T = 18: values agree when they differ by less than 0.0005 mm.
Motion outside OP blocks at or above the stock top (Z known and >= 0) is link motion and accepted: the first rapids, the move between the operations and the final retract.

Arcs whose end is exactly 0.010 mm from their start: not ambiguous (only 0 < |end - start| < 0.01 mm is refused), so they are ordinary arcs. The direction decides the sweep: the G2 sweeps almost a full circle, the G3 almost nothing.

Two full circles (red-team PHYS-16): a G2 whose written end equals its start, and a G3 with no X or Y, whose end is its start by modal state. End equal to start at file precision is a full 360-degree circle, not an empty arc.
Helical arcs (Z changes along the arc): accepted and linearised by later stages within 0.02 mm, with a note. The first is a full helical turn (end XY equals start XY), the second a quarter turn.
Blank lines (including whitespace-only lines) and plain comments may follow M30.
The reference program saved with a UTF-8 byte-order mark: the reader ignores one leading BOM, with a note, and line 1 is still the version line.

Lexical forms the reader accepts: words without spaces, tabs between words, integers without a decimal point, a leading plus sign, four decimals, a decimal F. Writers should still use the dialect's format (spec 05).
The example of the build design (section 5.1) as written, plus the licence line. Its Z values are in stock-top coordinates and are read as written: ZSHIFT -18.000 is informational and never applied.
The reference program with bare CR line endings: still one line per CR, as .NET File.ReadAllLines splits.
The reference program with CRLF line endings (Windows). Lines are split like .NET File.ReadAllLines.

Only the required header lines and keys (no ZSHIFT, no tool stick-out, kind, rpm or name) and no OP lines: operations are inferred by later stages and disclosed. job.toml's stick-out and rpm are not compared, because the GI header does not declare them. No M30: a program end is optional.
The reference program without a line terminator after its last line.

Accepted no-ops G17 G21 G90 G94 G54 G40; T1 M6 once before any motion, naming the declared tool; G43 H1 accepted and ignored with a disclosure; N words and coolant M7/M8/M9 dropped with a note; leading zeros (G00, M03, M05, M09).
The reference program: the full header (with ZSHIFT), one profile operation with a plunge, two feeds, a clockwise arc and a retract, then M5 and M30. The other examples change it in one place.

Three operations: a pocket with through=0, a profile with through=1 and a forced heading c=90, a drill with c=360 (the same heading as 0, spec 08). Labels carry UTF-8 inside the annotation, which is a comment. A plain comment that does not start with U or S is dropped with a note. Trailing spaces are ignored.
An unknown key (coating) on a known annotation: warned and ignored, not refused (versioning rule). Everything else on the line is read.

An unknown annotation keyword (FIXTURE): the line is warned about and ignored, not refused. Within version 1 anything new is informational by definition; a change a reader must understand needs version 2.

ZSHIFT -19.050 (the CAM had the stock top at Z = 19.05; it need not equal -t). The post has already applied it: every Z is read as written, so the plunge ends at Z -6.000, not -25.050 (red-team PHYS-12).

Z = 0 at the stock bottom (zzero=bottom), agreeing with a job.toml that says z_zero = bottom. Later stages shift Z by -T and disclose it; the reader records the header. Air moves stay at or above Z = 18 (the top).
